newsitem.title: BOSNIA: Princess Anne visits British troops in Bosnia.
newsitem.headline: Princess Anne visits British troops in Bosnia.

text.p: Britain's Princess Anne flew to Sarajevo on Tuesday to pay a visit to British troops serving in the NATO-led peace force in Bosnia.
Queen Elizabeth's only daughter arrived shortly before midday at Sarajevo airport to meet some of the 12,000 British soldiers enforcing the Dayton peace accords in the former Yugoslav republic.

The 46-year-old princess was scheduled to meet officers at the Sarajevo headquarters for NATO's Allied Command Europe Rapid Reaction Corps and British regiments under her honorary command, NATO spokesman Major Simon Haselock said.
The princess was also due to meet members of the Seventh Regiment Royal Signals and the Royal Logistical Corps.
Princess Anne was also expected to talk to Moslem and Croat members of Bosnia's newly-elected collective presidency. The British embassy said the meeting was purely a "courtesy visit".
The Serb members of the presidency refused to attend an inaugural ceremony last Saturday in Sarajevo's national theatre, alleging the venue was unsafe for Serb leaders.
Bosnian Serb forces laid siege to Sarajevo and shelled the city throughout the 3-1/2 year conflict.
